claude_analysis.tam_assessment: Niche market: the addressable buyers are EEG/BCI research labs and neuro-ML developers, and the existing catalogs in the data (EEGDash on Hugging Face, NEMAR, EEGLAB's tutorial data list, IEEE DataPort, GitHub awesome-lists) are all free; the Reddit and Product Hunt hits are unrelated noise, not demand evidence.
claude_analysis.pricing_assessment: No competitor price was observed, and the main alternatives (OpenNeuro/NEMAR, EEGDash, Kaggle, EEGLAB lists) are free, so ~$100/yr is an assumption that only holds for value-add like harmonized formats, ML-ready loaders, or lab/institutional licenses.
claude_analysis.legal_reasoning: The regulatory probe found no restriction signals and no government sources, though each dataset's own license (e.g. CC-BY, or a paid dataset like the European Epilepsy database) limits what can be redistributed rather than what can be catalogued.
key_risks: Free, academically backed incumbents (NEMAR/OpenNeuro, EEGDash on Hugging Face, EEGLAB) already do cataloguing, which leaves little room to charge
Buyers are grant-funded academics with low willingness to pay for discovery tooling
Redistribution is limited by each dataset's license, so the product may only link out and not host data
key_opportunities: Discovery is fragmented: search results spread across GitHub, ResearchGate, Hugging Face, IEEE DataPort and personal blogs
No incumbent shows funding, which suggests no well-resourced commercial player
EEG foundation-model and BCI ML work creates demand for standardized, ML-ready aggregated corpora
claude_analysis.value_reasoning: ~10,000 potential lab/developer customers x ~$100/yr ≈ $1,000,000 total addressable annual revenue.
claude_analysis.probability_reasoning: No ceiling applies because competition is rated 'contested', but free, community-run catalogs already exist and there is no evidence of willingness to pay, so realistic paid penetration is likely under 1%.
